## Council question

Who wins when Bene Tleilax infiltrates one or both members of a winning alliance?

## Why this needs a ruling

Quickstart v0.8 says Bene Tleilax wins alone if both infiltrated allies win with four strongholds, and describes an exception allowing the infiltrated faction to keep its ally with five or more. Another paragraph says no more than two players win.

## Answer needed

Resolve the cases with one infiltrated ally, both infiltrated allies, four strongholds and five or more. State how this interacts with prediction.

## Provisional drafting approach

Use a case table and confirm every winner set before adopting the text.

This is a research question, not an adopted ruling or a claim that Norbert has answered it. No answer has been supplied yet. Keep the affected rules provisional until Norbert or the council confirms them.

## Sources

Quickstart v0.8, Bene Tleilax Common Rules Clarifications and Multiple Win Conditions; [Live Bene Tleilax](https://dune.zone/factions/bene-tleilax).

Part of #1831. Record the confirmed answer, its date and a worked example here before closing. Norbert will share this link with the council; this ticket does not send them a message.

comments.body:
Confirmed by Norbert on 14 October 2026:

> 1 faction infiltrated, 4 strongholds: they win with the infiltrated faction
> 2 factions infiltrated, 4 strongholds: they win alone
> n factions infiltrated, 5 strongholds, the bt infiltration does not impact normal win conditions

**Rule (an alliance that qualifies to win):**

| Infiltrated allies | Strongholds | Winners |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 4 | Bene Tleilax and the infiltrated faction; the other ally does not win |
| 2 | 4 | Bene Tleilax alone |
| any | 5 or more | The alliance wins normally; infiltration has no effect |

**Worked example:** Atreides and Fremen are allied and hold four strongholds at the end of a turn. Bene Tleilax has infiltrated Fremen only, so Bene Tleilax and Fremen win and Atreides does not. If Bene Tleilax had infiltrated both, Bene Tleilax would win alone. If Atreides and Fremen held five strongholds instead, they would win together whatever was infiltrated.

How this combines with Bene Gesserit prediction is part of the ordered winner procedure, so it moves to #1847. Closing as answered.

Addendum, confirmed by Norbert on 14 October 2026:

> BG prediction determination happens AFTER infiltration.
> If BT wins via infiltration, and BG predicted anyone who won, BG steals the victory

So: work out the infiltration winners from the table above first, then check the Bene Gesserit prediction against that winner set. Example: Bene Tleilax has infiltrated Fremen, and Atreides and Fremen win with four strongholds, so the winners are Bene Tleilax and Fremen. If Bene Gesserit predicted Fremen (or Bene Tleilax), Bene Gesserit steals the victory. If Bene Gesserit predicted Atreides, the prediction misses, because Atreides was no longer a winner. Also recorded on #1847.
